clue.text: Where drinker might go topless once more for good measure

parts.note: a drinker heads off ... pub's bar, giving the phrase ... BAR

indicators.note: with its top removed, so the first letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: once more means again

explanation.surface: A thirsty drinker goes bare-chested back to the pub, an extra bonus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' cuts the first letter from AGAIN, leaving GAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in addition, as an extra on top of everything else.

clue.text: One cold diver raised main hazard

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a grebe is a diving water bird

explanation.surface: A lone chilly diver brings up a danger lurking in the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns GREBE upwards into EBERG. Main is the old word for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A floating mass of ice is a notorious danger to shipping at sea, hence a hazard of the main.

clue.text: Time to join barman's excursions

parts.note: a composer writes bars of music, so a barman is the composer Ravel; the possessive gives the S

explanation.surface: It is time for the pub barman to come on a set of trips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barman' is not a pub worker but a man of musical bars: the French composer Maurice Ravel.
explanation.definitionFit: Travels are journeys or trips, the same as excursions.

clue.text: Attempting to drop anchor finally when mooring

indicators.note: the named letter is dropped out of the word for attempting

parts.note: attempting means trying

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of anchor

explanation.surface: A sailor tries to drop anchor while tying up the boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' picks R from anchor, and 'to drop' removes it from TRYING.
explanation.definitionFit: Mooring a boat means fastening it up with ropes, an act of securing with knots.

clue.text: Sappers' manoeuvres

definitions.meaning: the possessive is read as plain plural soldiers
as a verb, manoeuvres means contrives or arranges cleverly

explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures army exercises, but the clue splits into two meanings: soldiers of the Royal Engineers, and a verb for contriving.
explanation.definitionFit: Sappers are military engineers, and to contrive or arrange something cunningly is to engineer it.

clue.text: See 1
Sign animal has tail removed

indicators.note: the final letter is cut off the animal's name

parts.note: a badger is a burrowing animal

explanation.surface: A creature's missing tail is a telling sign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has tail removed' takes the R off the end of BADGER.
explanation.definitionFit: A badge is an emblem or token worn as a mark of identity.

clue.text: Thinking son should replace daughter in centre of Berks town

indicators.note: the son takes the place of the daughter's letter inside the town

parts.note: Reading is a large town in Berkshire (Berks), west of London
taken as written

explanation.surface: A family deliberates whether the son should take over from the daughter in the middle of a Berkshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'should replace' swaps SON for the D at the centre of READING, a Berkshire town.
explanation.definitionFit: Reasoning is the mental process of working things out logically, synonymous with thought.

clue.text: Charge a posh car to go on main road finally heading north

parts.note: RR is short for Rolls-Royce, the classic posh car
the A1 is Britain's main road north, written AI

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of heading

explanation.surface: A driver is booked for taking a luxury car up the A1 northwards.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is the longest numbered road in Britain, running from London to Edinburgh; 'finally' takes G from heading.
explanation.definitionFit: To arraign is to formally accuse someone in court, calling them to answer an indictment.

clue.text: So-called leaders of next Olympics monitoring international news at Lausanne

indicators.note: the leaders of the words are their first letters, read in order

parts.words: next Olympics monitoring international news at Lausanne

explanation.surface: Officials heading the next Games keep an eye on world news at the IOC's Swiss base.
explanation.walkthrough: Lausanne is home to the International Olympic Committee, which makes the surface convincing.
explanation.definitionFit: Nominal describes something existing in name only, just as so-called does.

clue.text: Removing broken bearings after tip off

indicators.note: broken signals the remaining letters are smashed and rearranged
the first letter, its tip, comes off the word bearings

explanation.surface: A mechanic takes out damaged bearings once the end is knocked off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tip off' removes B from bearings, leaving EARINGS, which 'broken' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Erasing means rubbing out or wiping away, a form of taking something off.

clue.text: Sketch Indian city with simple housing

indicators.note: the outer word houses the city within it

parts.note: dim means simple, slow-witted
Agra is the Indian city of the Taj Mahal

explanation.surface: An artist draws a picture of an Indian city full of humble dwellings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'simple' looks like a description of the sketch, but it is the container for the city; 'housing' is the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A diagram is a simple drawing or plan that shows how something works.

clue.text: 4 Down reviewed information on church development

indicators.note: re-viewed means looked at backwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: the answer to 4 Down is a military corps; REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers
gen is British slang for information
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Army technicians look again at details about church growth.
explanation.walkthrough: '4 Down' points to a type of soldier, so a corps of army engineers is wanted; 'reviewed' means read backwards. 'on' places the later pieces after it.
explanation.definitionFit: The coming into being or rise of something is its development.

clue.text: Judgment ignoring sanctimonious tear-jerker?

indicators.note: the pious letters are ignored, so left out

parts.note: an opinion is a judgment
pi is short for pious, sanctimonious

explanation.surface: A critic's verdict dismisses a self-righteous weepie film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring' removes PI from OPINION. The definition is playful: chopping this vegetable makes your eyes water.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting this vegetable releases a compound that makes people cry, so it literally jerks tears.

clue.text: When breaking navigation system is pants

indicators.note: the small word breaks into the middle of the satellite system

parts.note: GPS is the Global Positioning System
as can mean when

explanation.surface: Losing satellite navigation is rubbish, says a frustrated driver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' looks like the British slang for rubbish, but here it is the verb to breathe hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Gasps are short breaths taken heavily, just as someone pants.

clue.text: Information published by Wimbledon committee about lake plants

indicators.note: the seedings list goes around the lake's letter

parts.note: Wimbledon's organisers publish the seedings, the ranked order of top players

explanation.surface: The Wimbledon committee issues notes about the plants beside its lake.
explanation.walkthrough: Wimbledon is the London tennis championship; 'about' puts L inside SEEDINGS.
explanation.definitionFit: Seedlings are young plants grown from seed.

clue.text: The French best-selling book is on the counter — it's passionate!

indicators.note: turned over the counter as in a reflection, so the run of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: la is French for the
the best-seller is number one, NO 1, written NOI
a tome is a big book

explanation.surface: A French bestseller sits on the shop counter, and it is a stirring read.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the counter' reverses the whole run LANOITOME.
explanation.definitionFit: Emotional describes being full of strong feeling, as passionate does.

clue.text: Mindful of voter bans in need of reforming

indicators.note: something needing reform must be reshaped, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An electoral reformer notes that bans on voters need overhauling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in need of reforming' rearranges VOTERBANS.
explanation.definitionFit: Observant means attentive and watchful, keeping something in mind.

clue.text: Mushrooms' creaminess changes without mustard at first

indicators.note: changes signals the remaining letters are altered in order
without means the letter is left out of the fodder
at first picks the first letter of mustard

explanation.surface: A chef finds the mushroom sauce's creaminess alters without any mustard added.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mushrooms' is a verb: grows rapidly. 'without' removes M (mustard 'at first') from creaminess, and 'changes' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To mushroom is to grow suddenly and quickly, so it means expands or grows.

clue.text: Country hospital avoiding hardline restructuring

indicators.note: restructuring rebuilds the remaining letters in a new order
avoiding means the hospital's letter is left out

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A nation's health service reforms steer clear of hardliners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoiding' removes H from hardline, and 'restructuring' rearranges ARDLINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ireland is a nation on the island west of Great Britain.

clue.text: Vintage singer is offensive

parts.note: cru is a wine term for a vineyard or its vintage
Sade is the Nigerian-born British soul singer

explanation.surface: An old-school singer is said to be distasteful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offensive' looks like an adjective but is a noun: a campaign or attack.
explanation.definitionFit: A crusade is a vigorous campaign, just as an offensive is a concerted attack.

clue.text: Dignified accent in Paris

definitions.meaning: the French accent ... is the backward-sloping mark over a vowel

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a refined French manner of speaking, but it is two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A solemn person is serious, and the French backward-leaning accent mark bears this name.

clue.text: Fast rider entertaining on a horse?

indicators.note: entertaining means holding within, so the answer is held in the words

explanation.surface: A speedy jockey is putting on a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertaining' finds the run inside fAST RIDEr. The question mark flags that sitting on a horse is only one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Astride means with legs on either side, the way a rider sits in the saddle.

clue.text: Unlimited budget ignoring the odds

indicators.note: ignoring means the odds' letters are left out

parts.note: to budget is to spend less
SP is the starting price, the betting odds in a horse race

explanation.surface: A spending plan pays no attention to the probabilities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring' drops SP from SPEND LESS. SP is the starting price in British betting.
explanation.definitionFit: Endless means having no end or limit, the same as unlimited.

clue.text: Involved in tense qualifying match

indicators.note: involved in means contained within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A player is caught up in a tense qualifying game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Involved in' finds the run inside tensE QUALifying.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to match something is to be its equal or rival it.

clue.text: Distressed to end term struggling

indicators.note: struggling signals the letters wrestle into a new order

explanation.surface: A student is upset at having to finish the term in difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' rearranges TOENDTERM.
explanation.definitionFit: Tormented means suffering great anguish, deeply upset.

clue.text: Charms without Mulberry's top bags

indicators.note: without means the letter is removed

parts.note: totems are emblems or charms

indicators.note: the top letter of Mulberry's is its first

explanation.surface: Lucky charms are left out of Mulberry's best handbags.
explanation.walkthrough: Mulberry is a British luxury handbag brand. 'top' picks M, and 'without' takes it out of TOTEMS.
explanation.definitionFit: Totes are large carrier bags, as in tote bags.

clue.text: Faultless late performance

parts.note: late as in former is ex
an act is a performance on stage

explanation.surface: A dead performer's final show was flawless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'late' looks like tardy but means former, giving EX.
explanation.definitionFit: Exact means precise and accurate, with no error.

clue.text: Close to developing angst about AI

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the inserted pair
developing means the letters grow into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Worries about artificial intelligence are nearly growing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developing' rearranges angst to AGNST, and 'about' wraps that round the pair. 'Close to' is a preposition meaning touching.
explanation.definitionFit: Against can mean right next to and touching, as in leaning against a wall.

clue.text: Greed from Aston Villa and Arsenal initially getting Declan?

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of each of the three words

parts.note: Declan Rice is the England footballer who joined Arsenal

explanation.surface: A football pundit asks whether Arsenal's signing of Declan from Aston Villa's rivals was greedy.
explanation.walkthrough: Aston Villa and Arsenal are English Premier League clubs; Declan Rice moved to Arsenal in 2023 for a record fee.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice is an excessive desire for wealth, which is exactly greed.

clue.text: Prepares bandages

definitions.meaning: a cook prepares or ... a salad or a chicken
as a noun, bandages applied to wounds are dressings; as a verb

explanation.walkthrough: Read as a verb, bandages means binds up a wound, so both halves are verbs.
explanation.definitionFit: To dress food is to prepare it, and to dress a wound is to bandage it.

clue.text: Secures number in empty turrets

indicators.note: in places the numbing agent inside the emptied word
empty takes away the inner letters, leaving the outer ones

parts.note: a number is something that numbs, and ether is an anaesthetic

explanation.surface: A guard locks up a figure in deserted castle towers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is read as numb-er, an anaesthetic, not a figure. 'empty' leaves TS from turrets.
explanation.definitionFit: Tethers means ties up or fastens with a rope, and so secures.
